messages:
olivia: Heads-up — customer reported unexpected KMS key usage in their audit feed. They claim a service account called svc-ingest rotated a key and decrypted artifacts outside their expected window. Can we reconstruct?

sarah: On it. Which customer and which key id? any example event they sent?

olivia: customer: acme-tech, key_id: projects/acme/locations/global/keyRings/main/cryptoKeys/ingest. They attached 2 log lines. Putting them here.

olivia: ```json
{"audit_event_id":"evt-01","user":"svc-ingest","action":"crypto.decrypt","resource":"key:ingest","timestamp":"2026-02-10T14:03:22Z","details":{"cipher_algorithm":"RSA-OAEP"},"schema_version":"v1"}
{"audit_event_id":"evt-02","user":"svc-ingest","action":"crypto.rotate","resource":"key:ingest","timestamp":"2026-02-10T13:59:11Z","details":{},"schema_version":"v1"}
```

max: quick check — our v1 schema didn't emit principal_type or auth_method fields. v2 added those. If any pipeline writes v1 logs they look sparse. Could be a schema gap.

audit-bot: Query finished: found 7 events matching key=ingest between 2026-02-10T13:50 and 2026-02-10T14:10 (query id q_892). Returning samples.

audit-bot: ```json
{"audit_event_id":"evt-00","user":"infra-ops","action":"iam.bind","resource":"serviceAccount:svc-ingest","timestamp":"2026-02-09T09:01:05Z","schema_version":"v2","principal_type":"service_account","auth_method":"oauth2"}
{"audit_event_id":"evt-02","user":"svc-ingest","action":"crypto.rotate","resource":"key:ingest","timestamp":"2026-02-10T13:59:11Z","schema_version":"v1"}
{"audit_event_id":"evt-03","user":"svc-ingest","action":"crypto.decrypt","resource":"key:ingest","timestamp":"2026-02-10T14:03:22Z","schema_version":"v1"}
{"audit_event_id":"evt-07","user":"svc-ingest","action":"access.grant","resource":"dataset:customer-artifacts","timestamp":"2026-02-10T14:04:50Z","schema_version":"v2","principal_type":"service_account","auth_method":"kms-signer"}
```

henry: Do we have a deploy/PR around 2026-02-09–10 that changed the logger? I remember a breaking change around RBAC metadata emission.

sarah: Yes — PR #345: "audit: switch to v2 event model" merged 2026-02-09 08:55 UTC and deployed in canary 2026-02-09T09:00:03Z. Deploy bot had a deployment at 2026-02-09T09:00:03Z -> commit sha c3f7a11.

deploy-bot: Deploy c3f7a11 to prod (audit-emitter) completed at 2026-02-09T09:00:03Z. Canary health: ok.

max: That matches: some services started emitting v2 after the deploy, but the ingest pipeline (where svc-ingest runs) still emitted v1 for a short period because it was pinned to an older docker tag during a rolling restart. So events around 13:59–14:04 are mixed. v1 lacks auth_method/principal_type so we can't tell the auth vector for decrypt events.

olivia: Customer is asking for timeline + proof they didn't get external access. We need to show which principals had access and whether any external user token was involved.

sarah: Action items: 1) Backfill v1->v2 fields for affected window (2026-02-09T00:00–2026-02-11T00:00) using replay of internal traces and IAM datasets. 2) Run targeted KMS key access audit for key:ingest and export full JSON for customer. 3) Notify customer with interim findings by EOD.

max: I can run the backfill job now. Query q_backfill_177 started 1769991400; ETA ~20m. Will attach output.

henry: Also open an incident ticket and tag legal/compliance. We should include commit + deploy timings as evidence.

olivia: Thanks. Please post updates here. If backfill finds decrypt events by non-acme principals, escalate immediately. :exclamation:

max: Update — backfill found no external principals for decrypts; all decrypt events correlate to svc-ingest and infra-ops bind events. Uploading artifacts to incident ticket INC-2026-87.

olivia: Good interim. I'll draft the customer note and attach the export.

sarah: We'll follow up with a small change to the deploy process so emitter can't remain on older tag during rolling restarts. PR queued.

olivia: 👍
